headline: Kimi K3 Plays Pokémon FireRed with Vision Alone: A Model That Explores on Its Own
summary: Kimi K3, an AI model, has demonstrated the ability to play Pokémon FireRed using only visual input, autonomously navigating and interacting with the game world without explicit programming.
details: Kimi K3, an advanced AI model, has achieved a significant milestone by successfully playing Pokémon FireRed. What makes this remarkable is its ability to operate solely on visual input, mimicking how a human player would perceive the game.

The model autonomously explores the game environment, making decisions based on what it 'sees' on the screen. This self-directed learning approach allows K3 to adapt to various in-game situations without pre-programmed strategies or explicit instructions.

This achievement highlights progress in AI's capacity for generalizable intelligence and real-time decision-making in complex, dynamic environments. It demonstrates a deeper understanding of visual information and strategic planning.

The implications extend beyond gaming, suggesting potential applications in robotics, autonomous navigation, and other fields where AI needs to interpret visual data and make independent choices in unstructured settings.

headline_marked: [[AI blamed for 600 Monday.com layoffs]] as tech job cuts hit 140,000 in 2026
headline: AI blamed for 600 Monday.com layoffs as tech job cuts hit 140,000 in 2026
summary: Monday.com announced 600 layoffs, 20% of its staff, attributing the cuts to an "AI-driven growth strategy." This adds to nearly 140,000 U.S. tech job cuts this year, as companies invest heavily in AI.
details: Monday.com, the Tel Aviv-based work management software company, announced layoffs of about 20% of its workforce, or over 600 employees. The company cited a "restructuring plan" tied to its "AI-driven growth strategy" as a factor in the job cuts.

Co-founder Eran Zinman stated the move was not to reduce costs or replace people with AI, but to adapt to an "AI-first vision." Monday.com expects $45 million to $55 million in restructuring charges, yet projects up to 20% year-over-year revenue growth for 2026.

This follows a trend where U.S. tech companies have slashed nearly 140,000 jobs since the start of this year. Giants like Amazon, Oracle, Meta, and Microsoft account for almost 50,000 of these cuts, as they funnel hundreds of billions into AI data center buildouts.

Interestingly, Financial Times analysis shows companies citing AI for job cuts have underperformed the Nasdaq by almost 10% in the 30 trading days post-announcement. This suggests market skepticism regarding the companies' explanations.

The picture isn't uniformly bleak, however. AI-focused companies like Anthropic and OpenAI are rapidly hiring, absorbing some talent. Within some cutting companies, headcount is shifting, with Meta moving 7,000 employees into new AI roles and IBM tripling entry-level AI hiring.

Other major companies have also cited AI in recent layoffs. Microsoft cut 4,800 roles, mostly in its Xbox gaming unit, acknowledging AI is changing how work gets done. Oracle reduced its workforce by 21,000 over the past 12 months, partly due to AI adoption.

GitLab laid off 350 workers to fund AI infrastructure investment and handle surging traffic from AI workflows. Google has also quietly cut employees across its Cloud division, including cybersecurity staff, despite significant revenue growth.
